summary: Two mechanical guardrails added under the operator's 'continue adding guardrails, verify and justify every change' directive. File-size guardrail (commit 57e32bc) — src/file-size.test.ts walks every wallet source file, console.warns files over 400 lines, fails the test on any file over 800 lines, per CLAUDE_ROOT.md lines 83-84. Keys-never-leave guardrail (commit 75033ec) — src/keys-never-leave.test.ts greps every wallet source file for console.* calls or web-storage setItem calls passing a secret-named identifier (privateKey/passphrase/seed/mnemonic/secretKey), per non-negotiable #1, the rule that outranks every other rule and previously had NO mechanical check. Both verified by deliberate canary — file-size by lowering the threshold to 200 (caught WalletProvider at 273 lines), keys-never-leave by injecting a console.log of the passphrase into createJournalEntry (caught at the exact file + line). Branch and main both at 75033ec.

why.text: Operator: 'Cut away make sure every change is verified and justified continue adding guardrails.' Re-grounded in CLAUDE_ROOT.md; non-negotiable #5 (mechanism over prose) plus the gate fence section ('When a rule matters enough to enforce, add a check') selected the work. The gate fence names five rules that matter — gates, keys-never-leave audit, tapit-attest integrity, feature-manifest coverage, branch gate. As of this session, four of the five are mechanical checks (features-registry, library-seam, plus the four base gates; this session adds keys-never-leave and the file-size rule from the Architecture section). The fifth, the branch gate, is explicitly a SessionStart hook concern, not a vitest test. Every change verified: each guardrail proven to fail-when-it-should via a deliberate canary before commit. Every change justified: each cites the exact CLAUDE_ROOT.md line it enforces.

files_changed: src/file-size.test.ts (new), src/keys-never-leave.test.ts (new) — two commits, plus comms
outcome.tests_passing: 19/19 across 5 test files (persona-contract, features-registry, library-seam, file-size, keys-never-leave). tapit-attest unchanged 82/78/0/4.
outcome.notes: Both guardrails pass clean on current code — no wallet file over 400 lines (largest WalletProvider.tsx at 273), no wallet file logs or web-stores a secret. The checks now stand guard for future regressions. keys-never-leave has two documented gaps it does NOT catch (transmits-on-wire, structurally prevented by the encrypt-before-network storage design; and indirect object leaks like console.log(wallet) which the by-name regex can't see) — both noted in the file's header comment, not silent.

uncertainty: The keys-never-leave check is a heuristic — it catches the dominant by-name developer-mistake class but cannot catch every conceivable leak (an indirect object log, a leak through a renamed variable). It is a strong net for the common case, not a proof of absence. The gate fence's load-bearing-review-surface guidance for any code touching keys still applies on top of the mechanical check.
next: The gate fence is now mechanically enforced end to end except the branch gate (a SessionStart hook concern, not a vitest test). The five named rules — gates, keys-never-leave, tapit-attest integrity, manifest coverage, branch gate — are all either base gates or mechanical checks. Further guardrails past this point would be inventing checks for rules the doctrine does not explicitly name as 'matters enough to enforce', which would risk cruft per non-negotiable #3. Lower-value candidates remain available if the operator wants them: total-post-auth-bytes ceiling (bundle-budget gap), manifest touches-array accuracy. Pausing here; the gate fence is complete.
